title: Breeding a sow by natural service
subtitle: Introducing the boar and confirming a successful mating.
excerpt: Natural service is the simplest and most reliable way to breed pigs on a smallholding. The sow is brought to the boar's pen for 24 to 48 hours at the peak of her heat, the boar is allowed to mate, and the sow returns to her own housing. Detecting heat correctly is the critical skill.
sourceNotes: AHDB Pork, Improving Reproductive Performance (2020). DEFRA Code of Practice for the Welfare of Pigs (2003), breeding section. Agricultural and Horticultural Development Board, Service and Mating Management in Outdoor Pigs (2019).

glossaryTerms.definition: The response of a sow in peak oestrus to back pressure: she plants her feet and holds still. The reliable sign that she is ready to mate.
When a sow cycles back into heat 21 days after a mating, indicating the mating was unsuccessful.

aliases: putting a sow to the boar

content.text: Breeding pigs by natural service involves reading the sow's oestrus cycle, introducing her to the boar at the right time, and confirming that mating has occurred. Sows cycle every 21 days; oestrus lasts 2 to 3 days. If you miss the peak, you have a 21-day wait. Getting the timing right is worth the attention.
Check the sow twice daily from day 18 after her last mating or last heat. Look for:
Swollen, reddened vulva. This appears 1 to 2 days before peak oestrus.
Restlessness: mounting other pigs or being mounted. She may also go off her feed slightly.
: press firmly on the sow's back while facing her tail. A sow at peak oestrus will plant her feet and stand rigid. This is the most reliable sign to introduce the boar.
Bring the sow to the boar's pen, not the other way around. Boars are more confident and less distracted in familiar surroundings.
Allow the boar to investigate the sow at his own pace. Do not rush or push them together. A mating typically begins within 5 to 20 minutes of introduction when the sow is in proper oestrus.
Mating in pigs takes 4 to 20 minutes. The boar mounts, achieves intromission, and ejaculates in a copulatory lock. Remain nearby but do not disturb the animals.
Leave the sow with the boar for up to 24 hours, allowing a second mating if she shows the standing reflex again. Return her to her pen after 24 to 48 hours maximum.
Confirming the mating and checking for

Record the service date in your holding diary. Check the sow again on days 18 to 24 after service. If she does not show oestrus signs and the standing reflex is absent, the mating is likely successful. A return to oestrus at day 21 means she is not pregnant; reintroduce her to the boar.

Pig gestation is 114 to 116 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days is the traditional rule of thumb). Record the service date and calculate the expected farrowing date immediately. This determines when to set up the farrowing area and increase the sow's feed ration.

attrs.cue: Sow shows standing reflex but boar shows no interest
attrs.cause: Boar overworked (mated too frequently), or a young boar lacking confidence
attrs.fix: Rest the boar for 48 hours. Do not use the same boar more than twice a week with multiple sows.

attrs.cue: Sow returns to service repeatedly (three or more cycles)
attrs.cause: Boar infertility, or the sow has a reproductive tract problem
attrs.fix: Try a different boar if available. Ask your vet to examine both animals if a second boar also fails to get her in pig.
